title: Runtime telemetry sampling RFC - architecture review notes
content:
Meeting: Architecture review for "runtime telemetry sampling" RFC
Date: 2025-11-05
Attendees: Maya Singh (owner), Ethan Park, Lina Rodriguez, Noah Kim, Priya Desai, Samira Alami, (observed: Miguel from console briefly)
Duration: 75m

Purpose:
- Evaluate tradeoffs and pick an implementable default sampling strategy for runtime traces & request-level telemetry that reduces egress/storage cost while preserving debugging fidelity for production incidents and customer-support workflows.
- Align on integration points (proxy vs. runtime agent), config model per deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), and rollout plan.

Agenda:
1) Quick walk through RFC goals and current telemetry costs (Maya)
2) Sampling algorithms reviewed: uniform, deterministic hash-based, reservoir + tail sampling, adaptive feedback (Ethan)
3) Privacy/PII and enterprise retention constraints (Lina)
4) Integration options and failure modes (Noah)
5) Decision capture + action items (group)

Notes / key points discussed:
- Cost context: hosted ingestion bills are growing ~35% QoQ due to long full-trace retention and high-cardinality metadata (model, route, api_key). Current rough ballpark: $160k/mo (ingest+storage+egress) for full traces; goal is to reduce 40-60% without losing SRE debug capability.
- We need different defaults for deployment modes: hosted (aggressive sampling by default), dedicated (moderate), private (respect customer retention config).
- Sampling goals ranked: preserve error/exception traces (priority), preserve tail-latency sessions, preserve representative coverage across models/routes/customers, allow deterministic replay for a sampled request id.
- Algorithms discussed:
  - Uniform sampling (easy) — downside: misses rare error classes and correlated-failure windows.
  - Hash-based deterministic sampling on request_id/trace_id partially solves reproducibility and per-customer rate control; predictable subset of traffic sampled.
  - Reservoir sampling per-customer or per-route to guarantee at least N traces per time window; comp requires state and memory but better coverage for low-traffic tenants.
  - Tail and error-triggered sampling: always keep full traces if error code or latency > threshold.
  - Adaptive sampling using upstream signals (SLO breaches increase sample rate) — attractive but more complex and risky for rollout.

Decision (consensus): hybrid approach (deterministic + tail + reservoir):
- Default pipeline will be: deterministic hash-based sampling at global default rate (2%), plus:
  - always keep full traces for requests with errors (status >= 500) or latency above 95th percentile per-route,
  - reservoir sampling guaranteeing minimum N=10 traces per minute per high-priority route/customer where applicable, and
  - a short-term adaptive multiplier for flagged incidents (auto-increase sampling by factor up to 10x for routes in incident windows).
- Rationale: hybrid balances reproducibility (hash), safety for errors (tail sampling), and coverage for low-volume tenants (reservoir). Adaptive multiplier is limited scope (incident window only) to reduce global complexity.

Integration & implementation details:
- Where to sample: two-tier approach  - Ingress proxy (node-level): perform deterministic hash sampling to reduce egress and route metadata early. Useful for hosted because it cuts telemetry sent to platform services.  - Runtime agent (model-server side): apply tail/error rules and reservoir sampling before flushing to traces pipeline. This allows runtime to keep fine-grained insights for token-level failures while conserving network egress. - Data passing: sampled full trace -> traces storage (low retention if not enterprise). Sample metadata/stats -> metrics ingestion (always aggregated counters for every request).
- Config model:
  - Global defaults controlled in control plane for hosted, editable per-customer via Console for dedicated/private.
  - Config keys: sampling.rate.global, sampling.reservoir.size, sampling.tail.latency_threshold_ms (route-level), sampling.error_whitelist (codes), sampling.adaptive.max_factor, sampling.keys (which fields to hash on).
- Privacy/PII: must perform PII scrubbing before any trace is exported to non-customer-controlled storage. For private deployments, default behavior is to keep raw traces local unless explicit consent. Add mandatory KMS tagging for enterprise exports.

Open questions called out:
- Reservoir state management: process-local vs. centralized? We debated per-process reservoirs (cheaper) vs. a lightweight coordination service for true global guarantees. Action: prototype per-process reservoir first; measure duplication risk.
- Adaptive incident detection: who toggles the adaptive multiplier? Proposal: incidents start from SRE/alerting pipelines (PagerDuty/Alertmanager) and from Console rollouts. Need a backed API.
- How to measure sampling coverage for low-volume tenants (signal that reservoir is under-sampling)? Define monthly coverage SLA metric (fraction of error classes captured).

Alternatives considered but rejected (reasons):
- Full deterministic only: rejected because it misses errors and tail events.
- Always-sample-critical-customers: privacy & cost concerns if customer misconfiguration; prefer opt-in with explicit retention agreement.
- Heavy-weight adaptive ML model for sampling: rejected for now given operational complexity.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- Cost target: reduce full-trace storage and egress by at least 45% in hosted baseline in A/B against current pipeline.
- Observability: SRE must be able to reproduce 80% of investigated incidents from sampled traces within the first 48 hrs of incident.
- No customer-visible degradation in debugability for dedicated customers with custom retention configured.
- Telemetry QA: ensure sampling headers preserved for deterministic replay across services.

Safety / fallback strategy:
- If sampling misconfiguration is detected (customer complains or major spike in missed incidents): allow immediate on-demand full-sample by route via Console (hotfix toggle).
- Telemetry guardrails: if a route sees >1% error-rate increase week-over-week and incident not acknowledged, automatically escalate sampling to 100% for 30m for that route.

Implementation plan & timeline (tentative):
- Week 0-2: prototype deterministic sampling in ingress proxy (Ethan) + basic config flag exposed to control plane (Maya) — PR #812 listed.
- Week 3-5: runtime-agent reservoir + tail-sampling logic + unit/integration tests (Noah + Priya).
- Week 6: internal canary on staging with synthetic load and fault injection (Samira + Lina).
- Week 7-8: limited production canary on non-critical routes (5% traffic) and cost measurement.
- Week 9: open rollout to hosted with monitoring dashboards + retraining of alerts.

Action items (owners, rough JIRA keys):
- Ethan: land ingress deterministic sampler prototype (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812) — JIRA INF-1454 — due 2025-11-19
- Noah: implement runtime tail/error hook + reservoir per-process (JIRA INF-1460) — due 2025-11-26
- Priya: add sampling config schema to control plane and Console UI mockups (Confluence + JIRA INF-1465) — due 2025-11-21
- Lina: privacy audit of trace exports and PII-scrub checklist (JIRA INF-1467) — due 2025-11-18
- Samira: test plan + canary script for staging fault injection (JIRA INF-1470) — due 2025-11-25
- Maya: coordinate rollout gating criteria and acceptance metrics dashboard (JIRA INF-1475) — due 2025-11-28

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: reservoir duplication leads to inflated perceived coverage (duplicate traces from multiple processes). Mitigation: add trace deduplication key on ingestion and sample dedupe metric.
- Risk: misapplied sampling causes missed security incidents. Mitigation: whitelist security-related events and always forward them.
- Risk: customers with strict retention requirements inadvertently use defaults. Mitigation: Console shows explicit retention prompt on onboarding and per-customer setting is locked for enterprise.

Decisions recorded (brief):
- Use hybrid: hash-based deterministic default (2%) + always-keep errors/tails + reservoir per-route + limited adaptive multiplier.
- Two-tier sampling (proxy + runtime-agent).
- PII scrubbing mandatory prior to export; enterprise retention honored.

Next steps / followups:
- Review prototype PRs in next arch sync (target 2025-11-12)
- Lina to circulate PII checklist and draft policy for review by Security team by 2025-11-13
- Schedule stakeholder demo (Console + cost delta) for GTM and SRE (target week of 2025-11-24)

Unresolved / longer-term items (parking lot):
- Evaluate centralized reservoir coordinator vs. per-process state (Q1 2026 investigation)
- Consider ML-driven adaptive sampling once basic telemetry and incident signals are matured
- Explore deterministic sampling keys that fold in model version and prompt-seed to better represent model-specific anomalies

Notes: this doc is a working record of the architecture review; RFC content will be updated after prototype results. Please add inline comments in the Confluence page if you spot missing edge cases.

Next meeting: 2025-11-12, 10:00am PT (arch sync)

End of notes.
